edits.english: It is taught [a baraita is taught]: Rabbi Shimon says: What is the meaning when the verse states: “And a second young bull shall you take as a sin-offering” (Numbers 8:8)? This is stated regarding the purification of the Levites after the sin of the Golden Calf. If this is written to teach that they are two, meaning that there is an additional second bull, isn’t it already stated: “And sacrifice the one as a sin-offering, and the other as a burnt-offering, unto the Lord” (Numbers 8:12)? Rather, one might have thought that the sin-offering for the Levites shall be eaten? That this sin-offering, which they brought for the Levites, should be eaten like other sin-offerings. To counter this, the verse states: “And a second bull,” which comes to emphasize that it is second to the burnt-offering and similar to it: Just as a burnt-offering is not eaten,

edits.hebrew: הכל עולה סלקא דעתך: והכתיב שעירי עזים לחטאת:

אף חטאת: דהקריבו לא נאכלת, לפי שהיו שעירים של ציבור הנשרפים, לפי שהכניסו דמם לפני ולפנים, כדכתיב: "וכל חטאת אשר יובא מדמה אל אהל מועד לכפר בקדש" (ויקרא ו, כג), כדתנן (זבחים דף מז.): פרים הנשרפים ושעירים הנשרפים, דהיינו שעירים של עבודת כוכבים של ציבור, דאמר רב יהודה: על עבודת כוכבים הביאום:

edits.english: Similarly, Rabbi Yosei said: It is stated regarding those who returned from Babylonia in the days of Ezra: “The children of the captivity who came out of exile sacrificed burnt-offerings to the God of Israel, twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve he-goats as a sin-offering; all this was a burnt-offering” (Ezra 8:35). And one might ask: All this was a burnt-offering, does it enter your mind to say so? Is it possible that a sin-offering mentioned there is a burnt-offering? Rather, it means that this is the intention of the verse: All this was done like a burnt-offering. Just as a burnt-offering is not eaten, so too, this sin-offering is not eaten. As it is taught [a baraita is taught]: Rabbi Yehuda says: They brought them for idol worship. And Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says: For that idol worship that they practiced during the days of Zedekiah.

edits.hebrew: ה"ג בת"כ: וכן היה ר"י אומר על עבודת כוכבים הביאום, ואתא לפרושי דברי ר' יוסי:
ואידך דב"ד: ואחד שהביאו בית דין, הרי שנים עשר:

edits.english: And now, granted, according to Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion in our mishna, you find these twelve sin-offerings in a case where twelve tribes sinned by engaging in idol worship, as they bring twelve he-goats (“he-goats for a sin-offering”). Alternatively, another possibility is that only seven tribes sinned, and the rest of these tribes are drawn after them. And according to Rabbi Shimon as well, you find the possibility of bringing twelve he-goats, in a case where eleven tribes sinned, as they bring eleven he-goats and the other he-goat is for the court. But according to Rabbi Meir, who says: The court brings an offering and not the public, and they bring only one bull, how do you find this case of twelve offerings? And they answer: For example, if they sinned and then sinned again, and then sinned again, until twelve times.

edits.hebrew: בין לר' יהודה, בין לר' שמעון, בין לר' מאיר: היכי קרבי הנהו חטאות? והא מייתי הנהו דחטאו בימי צדקיהו, דהוו חטאת שמתו בעליהן:

edits.english: And they ask: But didn’t those who sinned by engaging in idol worship during the time of Zedekiah, during the Babylonian exile, already die? And how can their descendants bring a sin-offering on behalf of their ancestors who lived in the days of Zedekiah? For their status is that of a sin-offering whose owners have died, which is not sacrificed on the altar!

edits.hebrew: לפי שאין מיתה בציבור: דאף על גב דמתו, ציבור לא אזלא למיתה חטאת דידהו:
אילימא מדכתיב תחת אבותיך יהיו בניך: דמשמע דבנים במקום אבות קיימי, וכאבות חיים דמו, והכא איכא בנים דדורו של צדקיהו:
אי הכי אפילו ביחיד נמי: לימא חטאת שמתו בעליה דלא למיתה אזלא, דלהוי הבן במקום אב:

edits.english: Rav Pappa said: When it is learned [as a tradition] that the law of a sin-offering whose owners have died is that it dies — these matters apply specifically to an individual who died, but not to a congregation, because there is no death with regard to a congregation, as the congregation remains in existence. And they ask: From where does Rav Pappa derive this? If you say from that which is written: “Instead of your fathers shall be your sons” (Psalms 45:17), and it is considered as if the fathers are alive, then if so, even with regard to an individual as well, the sons would be in place of the dead fathers, and they would sacrifice their sin-offering!

edits.hebrew: משעיר דראש חודש: דהוי חטאת, דאמר רחמנא דניתו מתרומת הלשכה, דכל קרבנות ציבור מתרומת הלשכה הם באין. והא דלמא מייתי להו מישראל לאחר שנתרמה תרומת הלשכה:
והנך: ישראל דפיישו:
היכי מייתו: שעיר דראש חודש דאתא מתרומת הלשכה, והא הוי חטאת שמתו בעליה? אלא שמע מינה וכו':

edits.english: Rather, Rav Pappa’s inference and his derivation is from the goat of the New Moon, as the Merciful One states: Bring them from the collection of the Temple treasury chamber, where the contributions donated by the Jewish people for the offerings are found every Adar of each year. And one might ask: But haven’t some people from the Jewish people died in the interim, from the month of Adar until the time the offering is sacrificed during the year? And if so, how can those who remain bring a sin-offering, since some of the owners of the offering have already died? Rather, learn from it that a sin-offering whose owners have died may be sacrificed in the case of a communal offering.
Which is a communal offering, and it is a sin-offering belonging to the additional offerings of the New Moon.

edits.hebrew: מי דמי שעיר דראש חודש: דלמא מתו מציבור, דלמא לא מתו, דספק הוי, ואהכי קרבה. אלא הכא דורו של צדקיהו ודאי מתו:
ראויה כפרה זו: בעגלה ערופה, שתכפר על יוצאי מצרים. וכיון שתכפר על יוצאי מצרים, ויוצאי מצרים מתים נינהו, אלמא אין מיתה בציבור. והוא הדין לדורו של צדקיהו, דאף על גב דמתו, מתכפרים בהנהו חטאות:

edits.english: And they wonder: Are these matters comparable? In the case of the goat of the New Moon, there is room to say perhaps no one from the public died in the interim. But here, in the case of the returnees to Zion from Babylonia, those who sinned by engaging in idol worship during the days of Zedekiah certainly died, for many years have passed since then! Rather, Rav Pappa’s reason is from here, from this verse, as it is written in the confession over the eglah arufa: “Atone for Your people Israel whom You have redeemed, Lord” (Deuteronomy 21:8), meaning: This atonement is fit to atone for those who emerged from Egypt, from the fact that it is written: “Whom You have redeemed,” referring to those who emerged from Egypt whom God redeemed from exile, even though those who emerged from Egypt died a long time ago.

And the Meiri brings a manuscript version that the derivation is from what is stated at the end of the verse, “And the blood shall be atoned for them,” which comes to teach that there is atonement for all, both for the living congregation of Israel and for those who were from the time of the Exodus from Egypt (“whom You have redeemed, Lord”). And some wrote that since the law of the eglah arufa was not practiced in the desert, but only from the time Israel entered the land, everyone needed this atonement from the time of the Exodus from Egypt (Arukh LaNer, Tractate Keritot).

edits.hebrew: התם: גבי עגלה ערופה, כולהו איתנהו בחיים, דעיקר כי אתיא עגלה ערופה אהני דאיתנהו קא אתיא. ומגו דמכפרה אחיים, מכפרה נמי אמתים, דהיינו יוצאי מצרים. אבל הכא, מי הוו חיים הני דורו של צדקיהו?

edits.english: And they still ask: Are these matters comparable? There, all of them are present at the time the eglah arufa is brought for their atonement, and it is possible to say: Since it atones for the living, it also atones for the dead. But here, were there any people alive who remained from the days of Zedekiah for whom their sin could be atoned by this offering? And they answer: Yes, it is indeed so that there were still people remaining, as it is written: “Many of the priests and Levites and heads of patrilineal houses, the elders who had seen the first House standing on its foundation, wept with a loud voice when this House was before their eyes. And many shouted aloud for joy” (Ezra 3:12).

edits.hebrew: ודלמא מועטין הוו: דהאי דכתיב: "ורבים מהכהנים והלוים", דלמא מועטין דציבור דבית שני הוו, והוה ליה חטאת שמתו רוב בעליה ולא קרבה, והכא כתיב דקרבה:

הא לא מצית אמרת דמועטין הוו: אלא ודאי רבים הוו, דכתיב: "ואין העם מכירים קול תרועת השמחה לקול בכי העם". ואותן דבוכים מדור של בית הראשון היו, ומדאין מכירים קול השמחה, שמע מינה דרובא הוו אותן דבוכים, והוי כחטאת שרוב בעליה קיימין, ומשום הכי קרבה:

edits.english: (Ezra 3:12), and it is found that there were still people then who lived during the time of the First Temple. And they ask: But perhaps those elders were few in number and were not many! And the majority of the congregation was from those who were not alive in the days of Zedekiah? And they answer: Isn’t it written in the following verse: “(And they did not discern the sound) And the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people; for the people shouted with a great shout, and the noise was heard far off” (Ezra 3:13). This implies that the weeping elders were more numerous than the younger people.

edits.hebrew: והא מזידין הוו: דורו של צדקיהו ובני קטלא נינהו, ולא בני קרבן נינהו. והיכי מתכפרים בהנך חטאות:
הוראת שעה היתה: דאף על גב דהוו מזידין, הוו מתכפרים:

edits.english: And they raise a more fundamental question regarding the matter itself: But they were intentional sinners regarding idol worship in the days of Zedekiah. If so, why should they bring sin-offerings, which are brought for unwitting transgressions? And they answer: It was a provisional edict. And they comment: So too it is reasonable, for if you do not say so, then regarding what is stated there: “ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs,” to what do they correspond? Rather, it was a provisional edict. Here too, regarding atonement for intentional transgressions, it was a provisional edict.
For it is stated that they were exiled because they sinned with idol worship, and this sin was intentional, so what is the relevance of a sin-offering for someone who acted intentionally (see Rashi).

That this atonement would be effective even for intentional transgressions (Rashi). And Tosafot noted that by this answer, that the entire offering was a provisional edict, all the questions on this topic were automatically resolved, and therefore nothing can be proven from here regarding the laws of a communal sin-offering for an unwitting transgression, as this was not an offering according to the law but a provisional edict, based on the prophets who were in that generation.

edits.hebrew: אילים וכבשים: צריך עיון מאי טעמא נשרפו, שהרי אינן באין על עבודת כוכבים:
הוראת שעה היתה: הוא הדין דעל כולהו מצי לתרוצי הכי:
